introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
enonce_intro_markdown: Chia, Mbako and Fru started a business with total amount of 350,000 FCFA. Of this amount, Chia contributed 50,000 FCFA, Mbako contributed 100,000 FCFA and Fru contributed 200,000 FCFA. The monthly profit they made was shared amongst the three of them in the ratio of the amount they contributed. Given that they made a total profit of 21,000 FCFA in the first month, 28,000 FCFA in the second month and 35,000 FCFA in the third month and that the profit kept increasing in this manner for the first 12 months,

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) State the ratio of their shares in the simplest form. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The shares follow the contributions: Chia : Mbako : Fru $=50{,}000:100{,}000:200{,}000$.

Divide every term by $50{,}000$: $1:2:4$.

**Ratio $=1:2:4$** (Chia : Mbako : Fru).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the table below and answer the questions that follow.

| Month | Total profit made in FCFA | Profit made by Chia | Profit made by Mbako | Profit made by Fru |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | 21,000 | 3,000 | 6,000 | 12,000 |
| 2nd | 28,000 | 4,000 | 8,000 | 16,000 |
| 3rd | 35,000 | 5,000 | 10,000 | 20,000 |

(b) Find the total profit made in the $12^{\text{th}}$ month. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The monthly total profit $21{,}000,\ 28{,}000,\ 35{,}000,\dots$ increases by $7{,}000$ each month, so it is an **arithmetic progression** with first term $a=21{,}000$ and common difference $d=7{,}000$.

$$T_{12}=a+11d=21{,}000+11\times7{,}000=21{,}000+77{,}000=98{,}000.$$

(The table is completed in the same way: the shares are $\tfrac17$, $\tfrac27$ and $\tfrac47$ of the total, and each share is also an arithmetic progression.)

**The total profit in the 12th month is 98,000 FCFA.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Find the profit Mbako made in the $9^{\text{th}}$ month. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Total profit in the 9th month: $T_9=21{,}000+8\times7{,}000=77{,}000$ FCFA.

Mbako's share is $\dfrac27$ of the total (ratio $1:2:4$ gives $\dfrac{2}{1+2+4}$):

$$\frac27\times77{,}000=22{,}000.$$

Check with Mbako's own progression $6{,}000,\ 8{,}000,\ 10{,}000,\dots$ ($a=6{,}000$, $d=2{,}000$): $6{,}000+8\times2{,}000=22{,}000$.

**Mbako's profit in the 9th month is 22,000 FCFA.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (d) Find the total profit Fru made in the first 12 months. *[2 marks]*
